data.name: Razeeyun
data.gender_notes: Razeeyun is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'razah' which means 'to draw near', and 'un' which means 'moon'. It means 'to draw near to the moon'. The name Razeeyun carries the meaning “Moon” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Razeeyun usually hope their child will grow to embody moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the connection between the individual and the divine, representing closeness to the divine and a deep sense of spiritual growth and development.
data.etymology: Razeeyun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Razeeyun total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: راضيون
in_arabic.long_meaning: راضيون نام کا مطلب ہے جو اللہ تعالی کی رضا و خشنودی حاصل کرنے والے ہیں۔ یہ نام رضا اور خشنودی کی طلب کے لئے اسلامی ثقافت میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے کہ جو شخص اللہ کی رضا میں راضی رہے اور اس کی خشنودی کو اپنا مقصد بنائے۔

in_hindi.name: रज़ीयून
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान की رضा और संतुष्टि प्राप्त करने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: रज़ीयून नाम का अर्थ है जो लोग अल्लाह की رضा और संतुष्टि प्राप्त करते हैं। यह नाम इस्लामी संस्कृति में महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है क्योंकि यह رضा और संतुष्टि की इच्छा को दर्शाता है। इसका अर्थ है कि जो व्यक्ति अल्लाह की رضा में संतुष्ट रहता है और उसकी संतुष्टि को अपना उद्देश्य बनाता है।

in_english.name: Razeeyun
in_english.meaning: Those who attain Allah's pleasure and satisfaction
in_english.long_meaning: The name Razeeyun signifies individuals who acquire Allah's pleasure and satisfaction. Rooted in Arabic, the term 'Razi' (راضي) implies being pleased or satisfied. In Islamic tradition, this name holds significance as it reflects the aspiration for spiritual fulfillment through divine approval. Historically, it has been used to describe personalities who embody contentment and submission to God's will. The name encourages virtues like humility, gratitude, and righteousness.
